# MCP reference

The tools `macos-harness mcp` serves, with each parameter. Errors end with `(error N)`; the codes are in the [interface contract](../../knowledge/design/interface-contract.md).

- [`doctor`](#doctor): Check setup
- [`apps`](#apps): List apps
- [`windows`](#windows): List windows
- [`snapshot`](#snapshot): Read UI
- [`find`](#find): Find elements
- [`screenshot`](#screenshot): Look at a window
- [`menu`](#menu): Read menus
- [`act`](#act): Act on an element
- [`pointer`](#pointer): Use the mouse
- [`steps`](#steps): Run several steps
- [`menu_select`](#menu_select): Choose a menu item
- [`window`](#window): Manage a window
- [`launch`](#launch): Launch an app
- [`quit`](#quit): Quit an app
- [`wait`](#wait): Wait for an element
- [`simulator`](#simulator): Run an iOS Simulator
- [`android`](#android): Run an Android device
- [`build`](#build): Build an iOS app
- [`build_status`](#build_status): Check a build
- [`record`](#record): Record an app on video

## Instructions

What the server tells an agent when it connects:

> macOS Harness lets you see and operate Mac apps. Typical loop: `apps` or `windows` to find the app, `snapshot` to get its UI as refs (like k12) with click points, then `act` on a ref (press, set-value, type, key…). Every action reports what changed, so you rarely need a new snapshot. Use `menu_select` for menu commands, `screenshot` to look, `wait` for things that take time. Refs end when the app or the helper restarts. Icons on the right of the menu bar are menu bar extras: `menu` and `menu_select` with extras=true list them, read their menus and choose from them (the system's Wi‑Fi, Sound, clock and the like belong to MenuBarAgent on recent macOS, Control Center before, and SystemUIServer). `act` works through accessibility and doesn't move the user's cursor; prefer it. When an element has no accessibility action, or you need a drag, hover, scroll or right-click, use `pointer`. Its clicks and scrolls go to the window in the background first; when that changes nothing, and for drags and hovers, it uses the real mouse (it brings the app to the front, puts the cursor back, and waits if the user is busy). Right-click returns the context menu's items as refs to press. A drag can end in another window or app: name it with to_app and to_window. For text the tree doesn't have, `find` with ocr=true reads the window's pixels (pointer accepts ocr=true too), and screenshot grid=100 draws coordinates for canvases. `record` captures an app's windows to a movie when the user should see what happened. Text fields often save only when editing ends: after set-value or type, send key tab or return if the change didn't show elsewhere. The user can stop you from the menu bar or with ⌃⌥⌘.; if a call says you were stopped, ask them to resume, and never restart the helper to get around it. Other agent sessions may be working at the same time: acting in a window (or on a simulator or Android device) keeps it yours for 30 s after your last step, and a window another session is working in shows "in use by" in `windows` and refuses your actions (error 1006) until that session goes quiet; work in another window or try again later. Reading is always fine. Keys go to the app's focused window, so `key`, and typing that can't go through accessibility, are refused the same way when that window is another session's; type into a named element instead. The real mouse and keyboard are shared in turns: real input (pointer steps that need the real mouse, and act with real=true) waits in line (a notice says how long), gives the front back to the app that had it afterwards, and fails with error 1007 if the line is too long; prefer `act`, which needs no turn. To run several steps you've already decided (fill a form, then press a button), send them in one `steps` call: you get each step's outcome and the changes they made. iOS Simulators (Xcode 27+): pass app="sim:\<device>" (a UDID, a name, or sim:booted) to snapshot, find, screenshot, act, pointer and wait; coordinates are then the device's points. Tapping, set-value and scrolling go through accessibility; pointer drag is a swipe and long-press a long press. Use `simulator` to list, boot, install, launch, press buttons (home, lock…), open URLs and change settings, and `build` to build an app for it. Android emulators and phones: pass app="android:\<device>" (an adb serial, an emulator's name, a phone's model, or android:booted) to the same tools; coordinates are then the screen's pixels and everything goes through adb, so the user's Mac and cursor aren't touched. Each read takes 2–3 s, so act on refs and read the change lists rather than snapshotting after every step. Only plain ASCII can be typed. Use `android` to list, start and stop emulators, install and launch apps, press Back and Home, and change settings.

## doctor

**Check setup.** Read only. Check that the macOS Harness helper runs, has its permissions, and whether you're paired or stopped.

No parameters.

## apps

**List apps.** Read only. Running apps, frontmost first, with window counts.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `all` | boolean | Include menu bar agents and background processes. |

## windows

**List windows.** Read only. Windows with IDs, titles, sizes and state. Omit app for all apps.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` | string | App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:\<device> for an iOS Simulator (UDID, name or booted); android:\<device> for an Android emulator or phone (serial, name or booted). |

## snapshot

**Read UI.** Read only. The window's UI as an indented tree: `ref role "label" = value id=… @x,y`. @x,y is the click point in window points. Use the refs with act. After a first snapshot, since=last returns only what changed since your previous snapshot of the window (refs stay the same), and query keeps only the elements that match and the elements they're in; both save tokens on big windows.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` (required) | string | App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:\<device> for an iOS Simulator (UDID, name or booted); android:\<device> for an Android emulator or phone (serial, name or booted). |
| `max_depth` | integer | Deepest level of the tree to read (default 40). |
| `max_nodes` | integer | Most elements to show (default 250). |
| `query` | string | Keep only elements whose label, value or identifier contains this, and the elements they're in. |
| `root` | string | Ref of a node marked "+N more" to expand. |
| `since` | `last` | Only what changed since your previous snapshot of this window with the same root, max_nodes and max_depth. |
| `window` | integer | Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window. |

## find

**Find elements.** Read only. Elements by text, role or id, including ones scrolled out of view.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` (required) | string | App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:\<device> for an iOS Simulator (UDID, name or booted); android:\<device> for an Android emulator or phone (serial, name or booted). |
| `exact` | boolean | Whole-text match. |
| `id` | string | Exact identifier. |
| `limit` | integer | Most matches (default 20). |
| `ocr` | boolean | Read the window's pixels with text recognition, for text the tree doesn't have; results have click points but no refs. |
| `role` | string | Role, e.g. button. |
| `text` | string | Label, value or identifier contains this. |
| `window` | integer | Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window. |

## screenshot

**Look at a window.** Read only. A PNG of one window (never other apps). labels=true draws refs on actionable elements; element crops to a ref.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` (required) | string | App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:\<device> for an iOS Simulator (UDID, name or booted); android:\<device> for an Android emulator or phone (serial, name or booted). |
| `element` | string | Ref to crop to. |
| `grid` | integer | Draw window coordinates every this many points, for canvases with no tree (try 100). |
| `labels` | boolean | Draw refs on the image. |
| `max_size` | integer | Longest edge in pixels (default 1280; 0 = full). |
| `window` | integer | Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window. |

## menu

**Read menus.** Read only. An app's menu bar, or one menu by path, with shortcuts and enabled state. extras=true lists the app's menu bar extras (status items on the right of the menu bar) instead; with a path, the extra it names is pressed to read its menu, then closed. The system's own extras belong to MenuBarAgent on recent macOS (Control Center before), others to SystemUIServer.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` (required) | string | App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:\<device> for an iOS Simulator (UDID, name or booted); android:\<device> for an Android emulator or phone (serial, name or booted). |
| `depth` | integer | Levels below the path (default 1). |
| `extras` | boolean | Read the app's menu bar extras instead of its menu bar. |
| `path` | array of string | Menu titles to descend, e.g. ["File"]; with extras, an extra's name first (optional when the app has one). |

## act

**Act on an element.** Press, set-value, focus, select, increment, decrement, scroll-to, type (text at the cursor) or key (e.g. cmd+s, return). Through accessibility; the user's cursor stays put. Returns what changed.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` (required) | `press` \| `set-value` \| `focus` \| `select` \| `increment` \| `decrement` \| `scroll-to` \| `type` \| `key` | What to do. |
| `app` (required) | string | App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:\<device> for an iOS Simulator (UDID, name or booted); android:\<device> for an Android emulator or phone (serial, name or booted). |
| `count` | integer | Repeat count for increment/decrement. |
| `diff` | boolean | Report what changed (default true). |
| `exact` | boolean | text must match the whole label, value or identifier. |
| `id` | string | Instead of a ref: exact accessibility identifier. |
| `ocr` | boolean | pointer only: find text in the window's pixels with text recognition instead of the tree. |
| `real` | boolean | type/key only: real keystrokes to the frontmost app. |
| `ref` | string | Ref from snapshot or find, e.g. k12. |
| `role` | string | Instead of a ref: role such as button, textfield, switch, tab, menuitem. |
| `text` | string | Instead of a ref: match label, value or identifier containing this. |
| `value` | string | Value for set-value, text for type, combination for key. |
| `window` | integer | Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window. |

## pointer

**Use the mouse.** Click, double-click, right-click, hover, drag, scroll, swipe or long-press. Clicks and scrolls first go to the window in the background, leaving the user's cursor and front app alone, and use the real mouse only when that changes nothing (a backgroundNoEffect notice says so); real=true goes straight to the real mouse. Hovers, drags, swipes, long presses and anything with modifiers use the real mouse, which moves the user's cursor (put back after) and brings the app to the front, so prefer act/press when an element has an AX action. Target an element (ref/text/role/id) or window-relative x,y; drags also need to_* or to_x,to_y, and end in another window or app when to_app or to_window names it (to_* and to_x,to_y are then in that window, and it must not be covered where the drag ends). Right-click returns the context menu's items as refs.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` (required) | `click` \| `double-click` \| `right-click` \| `hover` \| `drag` \| `scroll` \| `long-press` \| `swipe` | What to do. |
| `app` (required) | string | App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:\<device> for an iOS Simulator (UDID, name or booted); android:\<device> for an Android emulator or phone (serial, name or booted). |
| `diff` | boolean | Report what changed (default true). |
| `duration` | number | Drag: seconds the move takes. |
| `dx` | number | Scroll pixels, positive scrolls left; swipe: points the finger moves, positive right. |
| `dy` | number | Scroll pixels, positive scrolls up and negative down; swipe: points the finger moves, positive down. |
| `exact` | boolean | text must match the whole label, value or identifier. |
| `hold` | number | Drag: seconds to hold first; hover: seconds to stay; long-press: seconds to hold (default 1). |
| `id` | string | Instead of a ref: exact accessibility identifier. |
| `modifiers` | array of string | Held keys: cmd, shift, opt, ctrl. |
| `ocr` | boolean | pointer only: find text in the window's pixels with text recognition instead of the tree. |
| `real` | boolean | Click or scroll with the real mouse without trying the background first. |
| `ref` | string | Ref from snapshot or find, e.g. k12. |
| `role` | string | Instead of a ref: role such as button, textfield, switch, tab, menuitem. |
| `text` | string | Instead of a ref: match label, value or identifier containing this. |
| `to_app` | string | Drag into another app: its name, bundle ID or pid (default: app). |
| `to_id` | string | Drag destination identifier. |
| `to_ref` | string | Drag destination ref (from the destination app when to_app is given). |
| `to_role` | string | Drag destination role. |
| `to_text` | string | Drag destination text. |
| `to_window` | integer | Drag into another window: its ID from `windows` (default: to_app's focused window). |
| `to_x` | number | Drag destination x, relative to the destination window. |
| `to_y` | number | Drag destination y, relative to the destination window. |
| `window` | integer | Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window. |
| `x` | number | Window-relative x instead of an element (the device's points for sim:, pixels for android:). |
| `y` | number | Window-relative y instead of an element (the device's points for sim:, pixels for android:). |

## steps

**Run several steps.** Run up to 64 steps in one call, in order, stopping at the first failure, and get each step's outcome plus one observation. Write steps the way flows do, one action per object: {"press": {"id": "Seven"}}, {"type": "hello"}, {"set-value": {"role": "textfield", "text": "Name", "value": "Ada"}}, {"key": "cmd+s"}, {"click": {"ref": "k12"}}, {"scroll": {"ref": "k3", "down": 300}}, {"menu": ["Format", "Font", "Bold"]}, {"wait": {"text": "Done"}}, {"expect": {"id": "result", "text": "42"}}; add app or window to a step to act elsewhere. Every step goes through the same checks as calling its own tool. Use it for steps already decided; when one step's result decides the next, call the tools one at a time.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` (required) | string | App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:\<device> for an iOS Simulator (UDID, name or booted); android:\<device> for an Android emulator or phone (serial, name or booted). |
| `steps` (required) | array of object | The steps, as in a flow's steps list. |
| `max_nodes` | integer | Most elements in the snapshot when observe is snapshot (default 250). |
| `observe` | `changes` \| `snapshot` \| `none` | What to report afterwards: changes (default, every change the actions saw), snapshot (the window afterwards) or none. |
| `window` | integer | Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window. |

## menu_select

**Choose a menu item.** Choose a menu item by path, e.g. ["Format", "Font", "Bold"]. Brings the app to the front first unless activate=false. extras=true chooses from one of the app's menu bar extras instead, without bringing it to the front: the path starts at the extra's name (left out when the app has only one), and a path of just the extra presses it, returning the elements of any window it opens as refs.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` (required) | string | App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:\<device> for an iOS Simulator (UDID, name or booted); android:\<device> for an Android emulator or phone (serial, name or booted). |
| `activate` | boolean | Bring the app to the front first (default true). |
| `diff` | boolean | Report what changed (default true). |
| `extras` | boolean | Choose from the app's menu bar extras (status items) instead of its menu bar. |
| `path` | array of string | Menu titles down to the item; with extras, the extra's name first. |

## window

**Manage a window.** Activate, move, resize, minimize, restore, fullscreen, exit-fullscreen or close a window.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` (required) | `activate` \| `move` \| `resize` \| `minimize` \| `restore` \| `fullscreen` \| `exit-fullscreen` \| `close` | What to do. |
| `app` (required) | string | App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:\<device> for an iOS Simulator (UDID, name or booted); android:\<device> for an Android emulator or phone (serial, name or booted). |
| `height` | number | Height for resize. |
| `width` | number | Width for resize. |

| `y` | number | Top edge for move. |

## launch

**Launch an app.** Launch an app in the background (unless activate) and wait for its first window; optionally open files with it.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` (required) | string | App name, bundle ID or path to an .app. |
| `activate` | boolean | Bring it to the front. |
| `args` | array of string | Launch arguments. |
| `env` | object of string | Environment variables. |
| `new_instance` | boolean | Start another copy even if it's running; target it by the pid in the result. |
| `open` | array of string | Files to open with it. |
| `timeout` | number | Seconds to wait for a window (default 15). |

## quit

**Quit an app.** Ask an app to quit (force=true kills it; unsaved work is lost).

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` (required) | string | App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:\<device> for an iOS Simulator (UDID, name or booted); android:\<device> for an Android emulator or phone (serial, name or booted). |
| `force` | boolean | Kill instead of asking. |
| `timeout` | number | Seconds to wait for it to quit (default 5). |

## wait

**Wait for an element.** Read only. Wait until an element appears, or with gone=true disappears.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` (required) | string | App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:\<device> for an iOS Simulator (UDID, name or booted); android:\<device> for an Android emulator or phone (serial, name or booted). |
| `exact` | boolean | text must match the whole label, value or identifier. |
| `gone` | boolean | Wait for it to disappear. |
| `id` | string | Instead of a ref: exact accessibility identifier. |
| `ocr` | boolean | pointer only: find text in the window's pixels with text recognition instead of the tree. |
| `ref` | string | Ref from snapshot or find, e.g. k12. |
| `role` | string | Instead of a ref: role such as button, textfield, switch, tab, menuitem. |
| `text` | string | Instead of a ref: match label, value or identifier containing this. |
| `timeout` | number | Seconds before giving up (default 10). |
| `window` | integer | Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window. |

## simulator

**Run an iOS Simulator.** List, boot or shut down simulators; install, launch, terminate and uninstall apps; open URLs; press buttons (home, lock, siri, app-switcher, action, rotate-left, rotate-right); and set privacy, push notifications, location, appearance, status bar and pasteboard. To see and tap its screen, use the other tools with app="sim:\<device>".

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` (required) | `list` \| `boot` \| `shutdown` \| `install` \| `uninstall` \| `launch` \| `terminate` \| `open-url` \| `button` \| `privacy` \| `push` \| `location` \| `appearance` \| `status-bar` \| `pasteboard` | What to do. |
| `appearance` | `light` \| `dark` | appearance. |
| `args` | array of string | launch: arguments. |
| `battery` | integer | status-bar: battery level 0–100. |
| `battery_state` | `charging` \| `charged` \| `discharging` | status-bar: battery state. |
| `bundle_id` | string | The app, for uninstall, launch, terminate, privacy and push. |
| `button` | `home` \| `lock` \| `siri` \| `app-switcher` \| `action` \| `rotate-left` \| `rotate-right` | button: which. |
| `carrier` | string | status-bar: carrier name. |
| `cellular` | integer | status-bar: cellular bars 0–4. |
| `device` | string | UDID, name, or booted (default). |
| `env` | object of string | launch: environment variables. |
| `latitude` | number | location set. |
| `longitude` | number | location set. |
| `network` | string | status-bar: data network, e.g. wifi, lte, 5g. |
| `operation` | string | privacy: grant, revoke or reset; location: set or clear; status-bar: override or clear; pasteboard: set or get. |
| `path` | string | install: the .app built for the simulator. |
| `payload` | string | push: the notification payload as JSON, e.g. {"aps":{"alert":"Hi"}}. |
| `service` | string | privacy: photos, location, camera, contacts, microphone, all… |
| `text` | string | pasteboard set: the text. |
| `time` | string | status-bar: time to show, e.g. 9:41. |
| `url` | string | open-url: a web page, deep link or universal link. |
| `wifi` | integer | status-bar: Wi-Fi bars 0–3. |

## android

**Run an Android device.** List devices and emulators; start (boot) and stop (shutdown) emulators; install, uninstall, launch and stop apps by package; open URLs; press home, back, app-switcher, power, volume or open the notifications; grant, revoke or reset permissions; set an emulator's location; switch light or dark mode; rotate; show a clean status bar. To see and tap the screen, use the other tools with app="android:\<device>".

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` (required) | `list` \| `boot` \| `shutdown` \| `install` \| `uninstall` \| `launch` \| `terminate` \| `open-url` \| `button` \| `permission` \| `location` \| `appearance` \| `rotate` \| `status-bar` | What to do. |
| `appearance` | `light` \| `dark` | appearance. |
| `battery` | integer | status-bar: battery level 0–100. |
| `button` | `home` \| `back` \| `app-switcher` \| `power` \| `volume-up` \| `volume-down` \| `menu` \| `notifications` | button: which. |
| `device` | string | adb serial, emulator name, phone model, or booted (default). |
| `headless` | boolean | boot: no emulator window. |
| `latitude` | number | location. |
| `longitude` | number | location. |
| `operation` | string | permission: grant, revoke or reset; status-bar: set or clear. |
| `orientation` | `portrait` \| `landscape` \| `reverse-portrait` \| `reverse-landscape` \| `auto` | rotate. |
| `package` | string | The app's package name, for uninstall, launch, terminate, permission and open-url. |
| `path` | string | install: the .apk. |
| `permission` | string | permission: e.g. camera or android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION. |
| `time` | string | status-bar: time to show, e.g. 9:41. |
| `url` | string | open-url: a web page or app link. |

## build

**Build an iOS app.** Start building an Xcode project or workspace for the simulator with xcodebuild. Returns a build ID right away; poll build_status for errors and the built .app. run=true then installs and launches it on device.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `configuration` | string | Default: Debug. |
| `device` | string | Simulator to build for (UDID, name or booted); default: any simulator. |
| `directory` | string | Where to look for a project (default: the current directory). |
| `project` | string | A .xcodeproj (default: the one in directory). |
| `run` | boolean | After a successful build, install the app on device and launch it (needs device). |
| `scheme` | string | Default: the only scheme. |
| `workspace` | string | A .xcworkspace. |

## build_status

**Check a build.** Read only. Whether a build from `build` is still running, and when it's done: success, errors, and the built .app with its bundle ID.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (required) | string | The build ID. |

## record

**Record an app on video.** Start recording an app's windows (only that app's) to a .mov, or stop recordings you started. Recordings stop on their own after max_seconds.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` (required) | `start` \| `stop` | Start or stop. |
| `app` | string | App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:\<device> for an iOS Simulator (UDID, name or booted); android:\<device> for an Android emulator or phone (serial, name or booted). |
| `id` | string | stop: the recording to stop; omit to stop all of yours. |
| `max_seconds` | number | start: stop on its own after this long (default 600). |
| `out` | string | start: absolute path of the .mov to write. |
| `window` | integer | Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window. |
